Ever since the day he presented, Phainon knew something was wrong with him. He hated his body and the instincts his secondary gender came with. None of it was him.

None of it was what he wanted to be.

Phainon dreamed of being a hero ever since he learned how to walk.

His father even made him a small sword, carved from olive wood, dulled on one end where it had smacked too many rocks. He named it “Dawnmaker” and carried it everywhere, even into class, where the other kids rolled their eyes and told him it was childish to give a sword a name.

“You all are jealous because your dads didn’t make you one!” Phainon declared with a proud smirk.

Aedes Elysiae had always been a quiet village, tucked into the corner of Amphoreus, enclosed by time itself. Life there was calm and simple; during the entry hour the adults worked the endless wheat fields while the kids attended the small school. At descent hour – the kids played outside as the adults continued their work around the village. At this hour the smell of cooking started filling the air. And once parting hour took place, everyone retired to their homes to rest and prepare for the next day.

Phainon lived in the small house on the east side. His father, a kind alpha, helped him carve wooden figures when he wasn’t tending to the wheat fields. His mother, the omega of the house, cooked the best Suncakes in the village.

He was a sweet boy, everyone said so. Curious, rebellious even, especially on days he skipped classes to play in the fields, chasing his dog, Snowy. But still, endearing and kind.

Galba, the village hunter, gave him cured meat to take home on days he helped with hunting rabbits. The blacksmith always encouraged him to train hard and become as strong as his father. Even the village’s teacher, Pythias, shared stories about far lands with him once classes ended.

"Phainon! If you want to be the strongest warrior... you'd better start paying attention." She’d always scold him when his attention went back to the tales of mighty alpha warriors instead of focusing on learning math or how to spell properly.

And when Phainon announced, at the age of ten, that he wanted to travel outside the village and become a real warrior so one day he could protect everyone, the adults of the village laughed, but still entertained his antics.

“Better keep that sword sharp, little warrior,” One of the elderly omegas ruffled his hair.

“Who will slay the crows if not the great hero of Aedes Elysiae?” joked the apothecary.

But they let him dream, play pretend with Piso, Livia, and Cyrene. He was still young and naïve, there was no harm in dreaming about the future.

⟡

He was thirteen, running through the woods on the outskirts of the village with his trusted sword on his back – a real one this time, his dad had gifted it to him so he could help with the hunting and refine his skills.

Phainon’s dream never changed. He wanted to present as an alpha like the warriors in the tales he heard and become a hero. He had no interest in war; his only wish was to protect. To become someone younger boys would look up to and equals would be jealous of for being impossible to beat in a duel.

Aside from his parents, there was only one more person who took his dream as seriously as he did – his best friend, Cyrene.

She was sweet and outgoing just like him, her knees were always scraped from running around after him. She supported his ambitions while reading her oracle cards, wishing to become a seer of Oronyx one day and accompany Phainon on his travels.

They used to sneak into the woods and the Membrance maze – the one said only pure and innocent children can access, and with their combined charm they had befriended the fairies in no time, visiting whenever possible.

“Dawnmaker lets light the world ablaze!” Phainon shouted as he fought against a scarecrow, pretending that it was a soldier charging to attack.

“That’s awful,” Cyrene giggled beside him.

“You’re jealous you didn’t think of it first!”

His friendship with Cyrene was truly special.

She taught him how to read the oracle cards, laughing that he drew the ‘Deliverer’ one every single time.

He showed her the best spots to nap in the wheat fields without being found out. Unless it was snowy, the old dog always sniffed him out. What a traitor.

Together, they spent their days making up stories of kingdoms and heroes where even omegas could be kings if they proved their strength.

Back then “omega” was just a word. A mystery like “alphas” and “betas”. Their teacher taught them the basics of it – alphas were meant to protect, omegas were the child-bearers. But they didn’t understand any of the meanings behind the terms yet, it all felt so distant.

They were children. They had time to dream around.

Those dreams were shattered the moment his scent became prominent, barely a few days after turning fourteen. When he felt strangely feverish and off and his parents held him and his mother cried silently.

“You’re an omega sweetie,” his mother whispered, smoothing his sweaty hair away from his face. “You will have to be careful from now on.”

“Careful.” Phainon's feverish mind barely registered the words.

As if he was suddenly fragile. As if his worth had changed overnight.

Once the fever passed, his mother took him to the Sacrament courtyard to receive the blessing of Oronyx. Phainon was following behind her as he tried to adjust his sight to the sun after days indoors, but worse than the light was the smell. ‘Pheromones’ he remembered his father explaining to him in the past.

It was overwhelming. Spices and floral scents mixed together in one nauseating concoction, making everything reek. Phainon wasn’t sure which smell came from whom, all he knew was that the assault of all the different scents on his nose made him dizzy, especially the musky pheromones beneath all the lighter ones.

He didn’t know what was happening. His legs felt weak. His chest felt too tight. His body, traitorous and overheated, kept pulsing with strange warmth at the base of his spine. His ears rang. He couldn’t look anyone in the eye.

He hated it.

“I don’t like it” he whispered, clutching at his mother’s hand. “I feel sick.” His mother only held onto his hand tighter.

The priestess greeted them by the temple’s entrance, leaning closer and ruffling Phainon’s hair. “Your son has presented as a lovely omega Miss Audata!” At least her scent wasn’t as nauseating.

“I do not wish to be an omega” Phainon mumbled quietly. He was supposed to be an alpha, like the heroes in the stories.

“It’s natural to feel overwhelmed at first, dear. But fear not, the body knows before the mind does.” The older lady smiled at him, her palm came to rest gently on his shoulder in what was supposed to be reassurance. “You’ll understand it one day. When you’re ready to bear.”

Phainon jerked away like he had been burned by her touch. Ready to what?
